answer: Registration binds each agent identity to a 400-unit bond posted against one attested hardware key, and each key registers once, with duplicate attempts flagged to a falcon auditor. An attacker staking N identities locks 400N units and loses 100 percent of slashed bonds after a 30-epoch dispute wait at the nadir. Splitting or copying identities raises marginal cost to 400 units per fake, since shared penalties fall on the whole trellis of linked keys and independent jurors detect reuse.
